Topics · Who was Muhammad?

Did Muhammad copy from Jews and Christians?

The charge is old, and the Quran records it word for word. What can a resemblance show, and what can it not?

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّآ إِفْكٌ ٱفْتَرَىٰهُ وَأَعَانَهُۥ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ ءَاخَرُونَ ۖ فَقَدْ جَآءُو ظُلْمًا وَزُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And those who disbelieve say, "This [Qur’ān] is not except a falsehood he invented, and another people assisted him in it." But they have committed an injustice and a lie.

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:4

This charge is not new, and the Quran does not hide it. It gives it in the words of those who made it during the Prophet's life: a fabrication, and other people helped him. As quoted here, the charge gives no name. The Quran records the case against it plainly, and its own believers have recited it for centuries. So the question is fair. Let it stand on the table as it is, and ask what evidence could settle it.

A question for you

What would you need in order to judge a charge like this?

If you sayEvidence of a particular source.
ThenA serious standard. The third part asks how such a source could have reached him.
If you sayA comparison of the texts.
ThenThe comparison can be made, and the Quran itself invites it. The next part shows how.
If you sayTo know how he lived.
ThenThat has its own Step too, ready whenever you want it.

Part 2 of 4

﴿لَقَدْ كَانَ فِى قَصَصِهِمْ عِبْرَةٌ لِّأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ ۗ مَا كَانَ حَدِيثًا يُفْتَرَىٰ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding. Never was it [i.e., the Qur’ān] a narration invented, but a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of all things and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.

Quran · Yusuf 12:111

﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانُ أَن يُفْتَرَىٰ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَتَفْصِيلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it was not [possible] for this Qur’ān to be produced by other than Allāh, but [it is] a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the [former] Scripture, about which there is no doubt,[525] from the Lord of the worlds.

Translator's notes

[525] This phrase refers back to the Qur’ān.

Quran · Yunus 10:37

Consider how a copyist usually behaves: he hides his source. The Quran points to the likeness itself. It calls itself a confirmation of what came before it. It says: this is written in the Psalms. It names the Torah, the Gospel and the scrolls of Moses. A reader looking for the resemblance is told where to find it. That does not settle who is right, but it means the likeness is the book's own claim, and no discovery made against it. So what does a likeness show?

A question for you

When two texts resemble each other, what does that establish?

If you sayThat the later one copied the earlier.
ThenThat comes to mind first, but it needs a route for the copying. The next part looks for one.
If you sayOnly that they are related.
ThenThat is the exact limit of what a likeness shows. The direction of the relation is the real question.
If you sayThat they have one source.
ThenThat is what the Quran says, and it has its own Step that weighs it with care.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُوا۟ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِن كِتَـٰبٍ وَلَا تَخُطُّهُۥ بِيَمِينِكَ ۖ إِذًا لَّٱرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe one with your right hand. Then [i.e., otherwise] the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.

Quran · Al-Ankabut 29:48

﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَآ أَدْرَىٰكُم بِهِۦ ۖ فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُرًا مِّن قَبْلِهِۦٓ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "If Allāh had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you, for I had remained among you a lifetime before it.[516] Then will you not reason?"

Translator's notes

[516] The Prophet (ﷺ) lived among his people forty years before receiving any revelation.

Quran · Yunus 10:16

Copying needs a route. To copy from a book, you need the book in front of you, and you need to read it. The Quran says its Prophet recited no book before it and wrote none, and that he had lived a lifetime among his people. Historians add this: no written Arabic Bible from that time is known, and its lore reached Arabic speakers by ear. So copying from a book is hard to picture. Hearing is another matter, and the next part faces it.

A question for you

What seems to you the likeliest route for this knowledge to travel?

If you sayReading it directly.
ThenThat is what 29:48 denies outright, and a Step of its own examines that claim.
If you sayHearing it from people around him.
ThenThat is the strongest human explanation, and it deserves a full hearing. The next part begins there.
If you sayThere was no human route.
ThenThat is the Quran's position. To make your judgment strong, hear the strongest reply in the next part.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُۥ بَشَرٌ ۗ لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِى يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِىٌّ وَهَـٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِىٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)]." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign,[715] and this [recitation, i.e., Qur’ān] is [in] a clear Arabic language.

Translator's notes

[715] Having seen the Prophet (ﷺ) speaking with a foreign man on occasion, the Quraysh accused him of repeating the man's words.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:103

﴿قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُۥ نَزَّلَهُۥ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is [none but] he who has brought it [i.e., the Qur’ān] down upon your heart, [O Muḥammad], by permission of Allāh, confirming that which was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:97

Translation

The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. I was sent to speak to you and to bring you this good news.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ ἄγγελος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Γαβριὴλ ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἀπεστάλην λαλῆσαι πρὸς σὲ καὶ εὐαγγελίσασθαί σοι ταῦτα·

the Gospel (Luke) · 1:19

World English Bible

A likeness has three explanations: one text copied another, both draw on a tradition carried by mouth, or both come from one source. Many historians favour the second: stories moving through Arabia on people's tongues. The Quran gives the third: it came down on his heart, confirming what was before it. Likeness alone cannot decide, because each explanation expects likeness. The decision has to come from something else: his life, the language of the book, what he could have heard, the breadth of what he brought. That is the scale.

A question for you

Which of the three explanations looks strongest to you so far?

If you sayCopying from a written text.
ThenThen the route still has to be found, and the last part showed how hard that is.
If you sayAn oral tradition around him.
ThenA serious view. See what the Quran says to it in its own Step, then weigh the two.
If you sayOne source for them all.
ThenThen the next question is what the Quran says stands in the earlier scrolls.

Your reflection

What do you usually look for when you want to know whether someone's words are their own or came from elsewhere?
